page: Microsoft Azure F32amds_v7 is a memory-optimized server instance belonging to the Famdsv7 family, powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs on an x86_64 architecture, utilizing the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB per core. Additionally, the instance is equipped with 3780 GB of local storage and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage, though it does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU accelerators.

In benchmark evaluations, the F32amds_v7 demonstrates high-tier processing and memory capabilities. Its single-core CPU performance via stress-ng and single-threaded compression/decompression tasks rank in the top 10% tier. Multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth, both for cached small blocks and uncached large blocks, fall within the top 25% tier. Database operations, evaluated through PassMark, also reach the top 10% tier, while Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput remain strong in the top 25%. For machine learning workloads, the CPU-based LLM inference speeds for small and medium models achieve top 10% and top 25% tiers respectively, though performance drops to the middle 50% average when processing larger 70B models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the F32amds_v7 offers a high density of memory and local storage relative to its 32-core compute allocation, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads without the overhead of dedicated GPU hardware. The combination of a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC processor, 256.0 GB of RAM, and 3780 GB of local storage makes this instance suitable for large-scale database operations, memory-cached applications, data-intensive web serving, and lightweight CPU-based language model inference.
description: The Microsoft Azure F32amds_v7 is an x86_64 memory-optimized server instance from the Famdsv7 family, powered by a 32-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. It features 256.0 GB of RAM, 3780 GB of local storage, and supports Premium Storage under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Benchmark data positions this instance in the top 10% tier for single-core CPU performance, database operations, and small-model LLM inference, while its multi-core performance and memory bandwidth rank in the top 25% tier. Lacking dedicated GPU hardware, it relies on its high-frequency AMD cores for computational tasks. This configuration is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, large databases, Redis caching, and data-heavy web serving.
